messages.content: I need to start looking at flights from Atlanta to Denver for a gallery installation. I have to be at the venue by 8:00 a.m. Tuesday, August 19, so I’ll fly out Monday the 18th. The review on Thursday may end at 3:00, but it could run until 6:00. Please compare a sensible outbound and both a late Thursday return and a Friday return. I’m traveling alone, and don’t book anything yet.

I’ll keep both return dates open. For Monday, what time would you like to reach Denver, and will you be checking equipment or only ordinary luggage? That affects how much airport time I should leave before the flight.
Ordinary luggage, probably one checked suitcase. I’d like to be in central Denver by about 5:00 p.m. Monday so I can check in and get dinner before the early call.

The strongest Monday choices currently showing are: Delta nonstop, ATL 11:05 a.m. to DEN 12:25 p.m., $428 round trip with the Friday return; United nonstop, 1:10 p.m. to 2:30 p.m., $401; and Southwest nonstop, 2:05 p.m. to 3:25 p.m., $386 including two checked bags. All times are local. The Southwest arrival could put you downtown near 5:00 if baggage and ground transportation move normally, but it leaves little cushion. Delta gives you the most comfortable margin.
Set Delta aside as the leading outbound. Is the United flight enough of a cushion, or would traffic from the airport make that tight too?

United should ordinarily leave enough time. A 2:30 p.m. arrival allows about two and a half hours to collect a bag and reach central Denver by 5:00. That is workable, though a delay of roughly an hour would consume most of the margin. Delta’s 12:25 p.m. arrival is safer and also gives you time to deal with any luggage issue before evening.
Keep Delta first and United second. Now show me what Thursday night actually looks like if I cannot leave the gallery until 6:00.

From central Denver, a 6:00 p.m. departure from the gallery makes flights before about 9:00 p.m. impractical with a checked bag. The viable nonstop is a Frontier departure at 11:18 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 4:03 a.m. Friday. Paired with the Delta outbound, the current total is $472 before Frontier seat and checked-bag charges. There is also a United flight at 8:55 p.m., but you would need to leave the gallery around 5:30 at the latest, so it does not cover the 6:00 p.m. scenario reliably.
That overnight arrival is rough, and extra Frontier charges make the comparison unclear. What if the review ends at 3:00?

If you can leave at 3:00 p.m., Delta has a 6:40 p.m. nonstop arriving Atlanta at 11:32 p.m. The round-trip fare with the Monday Delta outbound is $446, and the checked bag is $35 each way unless your fare status or card benefit covers it. United has a 7:15 p.m. nonstop arriving at 11:59 p.m.; paired with its Monday flight, the round trip is $419, plus applicable bag fees. Both allow a reasonable trip to DEN after a 3:00 p.m. finish.
And give me two Friday options that do not require leaving Denver at dawn. I could work remotely for part of the morning.

For Friday, Delta departs at 10:20 a.m. and arrives Atlanta at 3:14 p.m.; with the Monday Delta flight, the round trip is $428 plus the checked-bag fees noted earlier. United departs at 12:05 p.m. and arrives at 4:58 p.m.; paired with Monday United, it is $401 plus its checked-bag charge. There is also a Delta 1:35 p.m. departure arriving at 6:29 p.m. for $451 round trip, which preserves more of the morning but gets you home later.

For now, summarize the two plans I should take to the gallery: Delta out Monday with the Thursday evening Delta return if they guarantee a 3:00 finish, or Delta out Monday with the 10:20 Friday return if they cannot. Mention the late Frontier only as an emergency possibility. No hold and no purchase.

Plan A, if the gallery guarantees the review will finish at 3:00 p.m.: Delta nonstop from Atlanta at 11:05 a.m. Monday, August 18, arriving Denver at 12:25 p.m.; return Thursday, August 21, at 6:40 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 11:32 p.m. Current round-trip fare is $446, plus $35 each way for a checked bag if no waiver applies. Plan B, if the review may continue until 6:00 p.m.: take the same Monday outbound and return Friday, August 22, at 10:20 a.m., arriving Atlanta at 3:14 p.m. Current round-trip fare is $428, with the same bag-fee qualification. A Thursday 11:18 p.m. Frontier flight remains an emergency option, arriving at 4:03 a.m., but its $472 combined fare excludes Frontier seat and bag charges. Fares and availability can change. Nothing has been held or purchased.
